title: Chmod Input
summary: Reads a Unix file mode back in plain words and flags permissions that leak data or lock people out, like a world-readable key.
description: Reads any mode (644, 0755, u+x, -rwxr-xr-x) back as rwx and plain words, and flags world-writable files, setuid/setgid, keys and .env files others can read, a writable ~/.ssh or authorized_keys, execute bits on data, 775 typed for 755 and short or decimal modes.
catches: World-writable files and directories, and setuid/setgid bits
Private keys and .env files readable by group or others
~/.ssh or authorized_keys writable by others (sshd StrictModes rejects these)
Execute bits on data files, and 775 typed where 755 was likely meant
Short, symbolic or decimal-looking modes, read back exactly
limits: Judges by the path and kind you pass; it can't see the real file, owner or ACLs
Advice assumes a typical Linux/OpenSSH setup; shared-group setups may be intentional (groupShared)
a11y: Visible <label>; aria-invalid and aria-describedby to the readback and report
Summary in a role="status" region; an unreadable mode uses role="alert"
Permission grid checkboxes have aria-labels naming who and which right
After a fix, focus moves to the next fix or back to the field
server: Set and audit permissions in your deployment tooling; this field only advises.

rules.note: Informational. Checked: StrictModes (default yes) checks file modes and ownership before login; authorized_keys must not be writable by others. Other per-file recommendations are conventions, not checked against a standard.
